page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the DLSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1D, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. This instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64ls_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core processing capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Geekbench multi-core score both rank in the top 25% tier, reflecting high parallel execution efficiency. This is further supported by strong performance in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for large blocks, with uncached read speeds reaching 292.88 GB/sec and write speeds at 135.25 GB/sec, both placing in the top quartile. However, single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core metrics, falls into the average category.

The primary tradeoff of the D64ls_v5 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which makes it less suitable for memory-intensive applications. Additionally, without a dedicated GPU, large-scale LLM text generation is weak, as evidenced by a 2.77 tokens/sec throughput on 70B models. However, its high multi-core compute density and strong memory bandwidth make it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks. It is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and parallelized CPU-bound tasks.
